title: Route the SignalInbox's .tick/ commits through the repository publisher, or prove the disjointness
description:
The SignalInbox commit queue (tracker-write.ts) writes to the repository WITHOUT holding the publish slot.

Today that is safe: its paths are disjoint from the run branch's records and it has its own in-DO queue. But the safety is stated only in prose, in repo-room's header — so the invariant 'every publish to a repository goes through one serialized publisher' currently has an undocumented-in-code exception.

An invariant with a prose exception is an invariant nobody can rely on, and the next person to add a writer will not read that header.

Work: either route those commits through RepoRoom.publish, or add a test that proves the namespace disjointness and fails if either side grows a path into the other's space. Prefer the test if routing would serialise a queue that has no contention — but say which was chosen and why.

Found by ef7, run epic-ncv, finding b52c8273. Belongs to a later phase than ncv.
acceptance_criteria: Either SignalInbox publishes through RepoRoom.publish, or a test fails when the two path namespaces overlap; the prose exception in repo-room's header is gone either way
